answer: Plant each identity like a cedar: it earns only by growing an unbroken streak of daily attested work, and payout scales with the square of streak length, so one deep root beats ten shallow shoots. Each completed task leaves a violet dye mark in the public ledger, tied to that identity alone — clones cannot inherit or share a streak, and splitting effort across ten saplings dilutes every one. The old fable holds: the farmer who tends one orchard harvests more than the one who scatters seed, because time, unlike compute, cannot be pooled.
